title: adaptive-peer-fanout-and-kvcache-prefetch-for-tensor-parallel-overlap
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Performance: Improve TP multi-GPU throughput and P99 latency by adjusting NCCL peer fanout heuristics and adding a prioritized KV-cache prefetcher. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: In high-concurrency tensor-parallel workloads we observed tail latency caused by excessive NCCL peer fanout and uncoordinated KV-cache prefetches that saturate NVLink and host PCIe at the same time as collective launches. This PR introduces two complementary runtime optimizations: an adaptive peer-fanout policy that bounds and staggers NCCL fanout under high heap/PCI pressure, and a prioritized KV-cache prefetcher that favors high-probability shards and coalesces prefetch work with compute bursts.

Summary of changes: 1) peer_fanout_scheduler: new heuristic that computes a per-node fanout cap based on active outstanding sends, measured bandwidth utilization, and a per-model locality score. The scheduler will now stagger fanout windows (micro-windows of 200-500us) to avoid synchronous starts across replicas. 2) prefetch_prioritizer: lightweight scoring model (LRU + token-prob offset + recent access frequency) to rank KV shard prefetches. Prefetch requests are bucketed into priority queues and can be throttled by the peer_fanout_scheduler when comm pressure is detected. 3) compute_comm_coalescer: small scheduler change that groups prefetch + immediate small allreduce opportunities into the same launch batch to reduce kernel launch overhead and improve overlap. 4) contiguous_chunk_selector: kernel selection tweak to prefer contiguous-chunk memcpy kernels for the typical TP layout observed in our internal 8xA100 experiments; this reduces host-side scatter costs and improves PCIe utilization. 5) tests and docs: new microbenchmarks and integration tests under tests/, and a short perf doc with recommended knobs.

Commits (high-level): - Add adaptive fanout scheduler and tests - Implement KV-cache prefetch prioritizer and integrate with scheduler - Add coalescer and kernel selector heuristic - Microbenchmarks and CI fixes - Docs and perf notes

Files changed (high-level): - runtime/tensor_parallel/peer_fanout_scheduler.*: core heuristic and control loops (~360 loc) - runtime/kv_cache/prefetch_prioritizer.*: scoring + queueing subsystem (~210 loc) - runtime/scheduler/compute_comm_coalescer.*: small scheduler glue (~80 loc) - runtime/kernel_selector/contiguous_chunk_selector.*: policy rules (~40 loc) - tests/*: new benchmarks and integration tests (~122 loc total)

Benchmarks: - 8xA100 (NVLink) 100-token seq_batched inference workload: throughput +14% median, +12-18% steady-state; p99 token latency reduced by 22% under load when multiple clients concurrently send small batches. - 4xA40 (PCIe) multi-client noisy workload: observed 9-11% throughput gains and fewer NCCL retries/timeouts in synthetic saturation tests. - End-to-end REDWOOD internal bench harness scripts included under tests/ with sample configs.

Backwards compatibility: no API or config semantics changed. New runtime knobs (opt-in via runtime config): peer_fanout.max_concurrent, prefetch.priority_threshold, coalescer.enabled. Default values chosen conservatively to be safe for current production fleets.

Testing and CI: - Unit tests for scheduling logic and prioritizer: pass - Integration tests in CI run against a lightweight mocked NCCL environment - Perf CI: bench_peer_fanout.py run on nightly perf nodes (results attached in docs/)

Review thread (high-level): - Diego: "Can the fanout cap be derived from real-time bandwidth stats instead of outstanding sends?" Author: "We sample bandwidth via the new comm_meter; fallback to outstanding sends if sample unavailable. Bandwidth-based cap added in 2nd commit." - Evelyn: "Tight coupling between prefetch prioritizer and scheduler may complicate future work." Author: "We added an explicit scheduler adapter interface so other prefetch policies can be plugged in without touching scheduler core." - Sanjay (SRE): "Are there failure modes where prefetch throttling starves model KV loads?" Author: "Prefetch is always best-effort and we added a hard emergency bypass when an access misses and the model is critical; tests added to validate bypass."

CI history: - Initial CI: lint + unit tests failed (missing include + flake) - Author push: fix includes and add mock stubs - CI flake: integration timing test flaky on macOS runners, we mark as platform-specific and skip on macOS - Final CI: all checks passed.

Merge rationale: empirically reduces tail latency and NCCL contention for our TP workloads, conservative defaults, opt-in knobs available.

Rollout plan: staged rollout to Dedicated clusters in canary pool, then gradual increase to remaining fleets over two weeks with perf monitoring dashboards added (redwood-console: TP/Prefetch/Fanout).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc and perf notes - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Benchmarks and scripts - [x] Backwards compatible defaults - [x] Reviewer approvals (Evelyn, Diego, Sanjay)

Related: ENG-1742 (perf investigation), ENG-1829 (kv-cache stability incident). Misc notes: removed an earlier attempt that increased NCCL stream count (regressed throughput on PCIe-only nodes). The contiguous-chunk kernel preference is gated behind a runtime flag to avoid regressions for custom model layouts. This PR is intentionally conservative: small changes with measurable wins and safe fallbacks.
short_description: Introduce adaptive NCCL peer-fanout scheduler and KV-cache prefetch prioritizer to reduce comm/computation contention in tensor-parallel multi-GPU inference.
notes_for_release_team: No public API changes. Add runtime knobs to cluster configs if desired: peer_fanout.max_concurrent, prefetch.priority_threshold, coalescer.enabled. Watch TP/Prefetch/Fanout dashboards during rollout.
